You said yes, so I'm staging this through New-Project Entry (§7). I've written no roadmap text yet. Here are the outcomes, taken from the spec's rulings and listed **unranked**, with their cost notes and a proposed track.

**Outcomes**

| # | Outcome (what you get) | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index table in Parquet for one real archived quarter, parsed from the SEC's `master.idx` | R1, R3 | Small in requests: 1 listing plus 1 file. Bytes and parse time are unknown until a real file is fetched. The core stage measures them, or the probe below gives the bytes now |
| O2 | The historical baseline over a quarter range you choose | R1 | About 300 SEC requests or fewer for the full archive: 136 quarters from 1993 Q1 to 2026 Q4, each a listing plus one file. That is under 2 minutes of request budget at 3 req/s. Total bytes and wall time are unknown. Older formats may also need their own fixtures, which takes your time and depends on the range |
| O3 | New daily indexes added on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 63 daily files per quarter, or roughly 250 a year. Catch-up cost scales with the gap since `daily.start_date` |
| O4 | Re-running the ETL from stored original bytes after a parser change, with no new download and no duplicate records | R6 | Storage holds every raw snapshot. Its size is O2's bytes plus about one quarterly snapshot per changed file per week |
| O5 | Weekly quarterly corrections: additions and changed fields publish automatically, and records that disappear leave the catalog only after you approve that exact source hash | R7, R10 | About 136 file requests per weekly run if every supported quarter is refreshed. Your time goes to each withdrawal approval. How often approvals come up is unknown until real reconciliation runs |
| O6 | Readers always see a complete quarter through one active pointer, never partly written files | R9 | No material cost |
| O7 | Backfill, daily ingestion and corrections can run together and never exceed one shared SEC budget of 3 req/s | R8, R11 | No compute cost. The SEC publishes a ceiling of 10 req/s per user, and the spec's target is 3 req/s |
| O8 | The pipeline runs on Azure on a schedule (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor) with alerts, runbooks and rollback | R4, R11 | Azure spend can't be estimated without sizing, and the spec leaves sizing to the deployment smoke test (§7 step 4). This is measured, not estimated |

**Tracks.** I propose a single track, **A, a known progression**. Each outcome builds on the catalog from O1: corrections, replay and the pointer all act on that catalog, and Azure is where it runs. I found no pair of outcomes that answers unrelated questions, so I haven't split them. If you see O8 (Azure) as a separate decision because the ADR is still *Proposed*, tell me and I'll make it its own track.

**Choices already made**
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`) in a uv workspace.
- The spec puts the code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The other three scaffolds (`-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`) aren't mentioned in the spec, and I'm not assigning them anything.
- Platform: Azure, as R4 and the ADR describe. Both the ADR and the spec are still PROPOSED, so I'm treating this as a choice only if you confirm it.

**Roadmap name:** `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`, using the spec's own stem.

**Optional probe.** I can fetch one real `full-index/<year>/<qtr>/index.json` listing to get actual file sizes for the O1 and O2 cost notes. This makes one SEC request, and it needs a User-Agent identity, an organization or name plus a contact email, that you give me for `sec.user_agent`. I'll only run it if you say yes.

**Please rank O1–O8, confirm one known-progression track (or split O8 out), and tell me whether the Azure platform counts as decided.**
